title: Quantitative Latin metre as a joint constraint on complete unknown readings
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A coherent portion could contain technical Latin hexameters; a bounded shared writing rule must simultaneously recover complete wording, grammar, lexical quantities and verse boundaries. This is not a claim that Voynich is verse, Latin, or a copy of Macer.

design.motivation: A hypothetical multi-scribe workshop might transmit a learnable technical verse text. Independently, the British Library catalogues a twelfth-century Macer herbal in Latin hexameters; this establishes historical availability of the genre, not a Voynich connection.
design.observable_contract: For one prospectively fixed complete target portion, every written element must be handled by one bounded shared writing rule. The same output must satisfy fixed lexical and grammatical constraints plus quantitative hexameter scansion. Do not equate physical writing lines with verses; boundary inference must itself have a fixed finite rule and account for the whole passage. No padding, omitted words, per-line keys, invented quantities or post-result licenses.
design.meaning_output: Complete concrete Latin sentences and their German translations, the explicit writing key, and syllable-by-syllable scansion. Any alternative grammatical metrical plaintext must remain visible; meter compatibility is not lexical identification.
design.decisive_prediction: After freezing the key, writing rule, allowed quantity variants and verse-boundary procedure, decode a separately reserved complete passage with no adjustment. Require agreement of all retained models on its full wording and scansion; evaluate competing nonmetrical and matched pseudo-text explanations under the same discovery procedure. This criterion is not claimed to have passed.
design.preimplementation_discriminator: Only after a manuscript-motivated bounded writing rule is actually specified, one independent six-verse historical challenge with removed verse boundaries and withheld key can ask whether materially different complete grammatical metrical readings remain. This is a finite identifiability decision, not a license for a control-repair series. Passing would show method feasibility only.
predecessors: GDT884 tested eight fixed Laufenberg introductory source strings under an erasing STA expansion and excluded all24 equations. That particular copy/code model remains closed. Its primary report corrects the older odd-physical-line objection but establishes no Voynich verse segmentation.
The earlier f85r2 Laufenberg rhyme-couplet capacity card is not quantitative metre-guided recovery of unknown wording. Missing keyword matches do not prove global novelty.

GDT906 already has zero grammar-accepted keys under the fixed892 CV channel and reference grammar. Adding metre to that unchanged empty model cannot recover a solution. This proposal does not reopen or silently repair it.

GDT832-837 show why plausible language scores and successful synthetic subchecks cannot identify Voynich plaintext. The proposed challenge must not become another optimizer or reference-corpus repair chain.
missing_inputs: No independent evidence that any nominated Voynich portion contains verse or Latin.
No manuscript-motivated bounded writing rule selected; more decoder freedom is not evidence.
No frozen complete target portion or finite verse-boundary procedure.
No source-bound quantity lexicon with fixed treatment of medieval spellings and uncertain quantities.
No feasibility or uniqueness result and no concrete Voynich reading.
design.claim_limit: Raw research idea only. No experiment, control, held-data access, semantic score, word meaning or translation is authorized by retaining this card. Existing route and GDT388 requirements still govern experimental selection.
